analysis.investment_thesis: Beezaasan scores decently on ROC (~22.8%) but weakly on earnings yield (EBIT 23 Cr / EV ~310 Cr ≈ 7.4%), so it fails the Magic Formula "cheap AND good" test. Persistently negative free cash flow (-12 Cr in 2025) despite recent IPO-funded equity boost makes this a wait-and-see, not a buy.
key_strengths: ROCE 22.8% and ROE 20.2% — respectable returns on capital for an explosives maker
EBIT CAGR of 56.5% and net profit CAGR 67% (FY22→FY25), operating leverage kicking in
Post-IPO balance sheet de-levered: reserves jumped 14→92 Cr, borrowings cut 37→25 Cr
key_risks: Earnings yield ~7.4% (EBIT 23 / EV ~310 Cr) — too expensive on Magic Formula basis
FCF negative every year 2022-2025; investing CF -35 Cr in 2025 signals capex-heavy cycle
Small-cap explosives player (Mcap 288 Cr) with low FII/DII float and short listed history
red_flags: FCF has been negative for 4 consecutive years despite rising EBIT
P/E 22.4x on a cyclical, capex-heavy commodity business is not a bargain
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: ROC proxy using EBIT 23 Cr over (equity 105 + debt 25 - cash-ish) ~130 Cr operating capital gives ~17-22%, consistent with the reported 22.8% ROCE — that clears the "good business" bar but is not top-decile. Earnings yield, however, is the problem: EBIT 23 / EV ≈ 310 Cr = ~7.4%, well below my 12% attractive threshold. The stock is priced like a quality compounder (P/E 22.4) without yet having proven consistent cash conversion.

The capex cycle is the swing factor. CWIP rose from 2 to 13 Cr and investing CF was -35 Cr in 2025, funded by a 48 Cr financing inflow (likely the IPO). If this capacity expansion translates EBIT from 23 Cr to, say, 40+ Cr while holding ROCE, the earnings yield re-rates and this becomes interesting. Until then, ranked against the broader universe, Beezaasan is mediocre-cheap with decent-but-not-excellent returns — a hold, not the systematic buy the Magic Formula demands.
